# Outward threshold smoothing: singleton sources and linked facet selectors

This is a NEW attained body-only variational problem approximating the H
problem. Its positive-width caps are smooth, so its actual common separator
retains the inside supporting contribution in the zero-width limit. No
arbitrary Clarke selection is assumed. The positive-width source set has
at most one base of each parity. The conclusion is a variational interface,
not a Gamma/k payment.

Dependencies are the compact original minimal-bad-base normalization,
ordinary projective-energy continuity/envelope, and actual convex physical
field construction already checked in:

- `candidate 26455afca6af9c16`;
- `candidate 8effe5eb4947ba88`;
- `candidate 714f69e684c396b1`
  for normal-bundle surface convergence and the already proved limiting
  Gauss--Green linkage. That identity alone is not claimed as new.

The source-parity step has independent proofs in
`candidate f32b13bc6996e859` and
`candidate 54bd04196c016a99`.

## 1. ONE outward kernel and an invariant width

Use the ONE outward UNIFORM kernel

    psi(t)=1_(-1,0)(t), Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)).

Thus

    Psi=0 on (-infinity,-1], Psi=1 on [0,infinity),
    1-Psi(t)=Psi(-1-t).                                  (1)

Although Psi itself has two corners, the cap integral (2) below is C1 in
its nonvertical plane parameters. At fixed u!=0, the two kink hyperplanes
have zero d-volume on EVERY positive sampled fiber. Dominated differentiation
therefore applies. The resulting strip integral is continuous under moving
parameters and positive-body Hausdorff limits, again because those two
limiting planes have zero volume. The body-shape derivative requires only
continuous Psi. No second derivative of the kernel is used.

Alternatively a C-infinity density positive on (-1,0), symmetric about
-1/2 and zero elsewhere gives all conclusions through Section 7 and the
quasiconcave version of Section 8. The UNIFORM choice is required for the
stronger one-height convex lifts in Section 8.

Let h>0 be the smoothing width, distinct from the H buffer epsilon. Write
f=H/M^(1/d) and Gamma_K(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma_K u), exactly as in the H problem.
For u!=0 and N=(a,u), define

    Q_h(K;N,c)=integral_S Psi((N.w-c)/(h Gamma_K(u)))dmu.  (2)

At a mark Y, use c=N.Y-epsilon f(Y)Gamma_K(u). Pure-base caps u=0 remain
ordinary closed pure-base caps; (2) is never evaluated at u=0. Minimize
over all these caps, maximize over actual mixed marks, and divide by M to
obtain beta_(epsilon,h)(K).

Both the buffer and the smoothing width scale with Gamma. Consequently
positive rescaling of a cap normal, common continuous affine maps, affine
continuous base shears, and unimodular base changes preserve the normalized
problem. A fixed Euclidean width would not have this invariance.

The outward direction of (1) is essential. Fubini gives

    Q_h(N,c)=integral_-1^0 psi(t) mu{N.w>=c+h Gamma(u)t}dt,

so Q_h(N,c)>=mu{N.w>=c}; nonvertical boundary planes have zero mixed volume.
Therefore GLOBALLY, before any compact normalization,

    beta_(epsilon,h)>=beta^H_epsilon>=beta_0.             (3)

A symmetric threshold kernel would not supply this implication. Using a
uniform slab estimate to establish a compact sublevel in that case would
be circular unless another global estimate were supplied.

## 2. Actual attainment and compact active menus

Fix sufficiently small epsilon>0 and a strict bad trial family for the H
problem. For sufficiently small h, its smoothed value is still below the
chosen original bad-sublevel threshold b. By (3), every minimizing sequence
belongs to the original compact normalized class A. Thus M=1, all volumes
have a positive floor, bodies lie in a fixed ball, and Sigma has uniform
positive lower and upper bounds.

On A, every smoothed cap differs from its unsmoothed counterpart only in
a slab of width at most h sqrt(lambda_+) for Euclidean unit u. The uniform
section bound gives, uniformly in marks and ALL base tilts,

    0<=beta_(epsilon,h)-beta^H_epsilon<=C h.              (4)

The cap functional is continuous under simultaneous positive-body
Hausdorff convergence, covariance convergence and moving marks. The same
symmetric-difference/slab comparison is uniform over base tilts. Hence its
infimum over caps and maximum over sampled compact fibers are continuous.
Affine invariance and compactness prove an ACTUAL unrestricted body
minimum at each sufficiently small fixed (epsilon,h).

The source-core and pure-base-gap proofs for H are unchanged with an
additional C h error. For epsilon,h small, every smoothed deepest mark has
a common own inball. Its buffered own plane and its entire width-h slab
are proper with a uniform section lower bound. Pure-base depth exceeds the
smoothed maximum Q=M beta by a uniform positive amount. Thus no active
pure-base caps occur.

Compact support of psi also preserves EXACT finite tilt clipping. Once a
fiber's margin lies outside the interval [-h Gamma,0], its smoothed capture
is identically zero or one. The old finite minimum-norm representative
argument applies with these slightly enlarged saturation margins. After
normalizing Gamma(u)=1, near-active caps have bounded representatives of
a and c. Active caps are attained; their parameter set is compact.

For every active cap put

    q(w)=(N.w-c)/h,
    S=integral_S psi(q)/h dmu,
    m=integral_S w psi(q)/h dmu,
    A=integral_S q psi(q)dmu.                            (5)

Here S is its positive smooth threshold coarea. Uniform own properness
and the global section bound give

    0<S_min<=S<=S_max,
    -h S<=A<=0.                                         (6)

For this uniform kernel, S is exactly the original mixed volume of the
open slab c-h<N.w<c, divided by h; A/S is its average margin N.w-c.
The last bound follows from -1<=q<=0 wherever psi(q)>0. In particular
ALL width corrections below are uniformly O(h), including near supporting
facets of other fibers.

## 3. Strict quantiles, exact section centroids, and parity separation

For a fixed nonvertical N, let c_Q(N) be the right Q-quantile of (2).
The actual depth-Q superlevel constraints are

    N.Y-epsilon f(Y)Gamma(u)<=c_Q(N),                   (7)

together with the pure-base constraints. These are convex because f is
concave on the actual canonical body.

At an attained active cap, S>0 means that the tail is STRICTLY decreasing
on a neighborhood of its through-mark threshold. A globally nonincreasing
tail cannot take the same Q value at another threshold outside that
neighborhood. Thus this active threshold equals the unique Q-quantile;
no plateau endpoint ambiguity enters the following equalities.

The cap minimizes over the unrestricted base normal a at its source
Y=(p,y). Since neither f(Y) nor Gamma(u) depends on a, differentiation gives

    m_base=S p.                                         (8)

Differentiating in u, while remembering BOTH occurrences of Gamma, gives

    m_cont/S = y-[epsilon f(Y)-A/S] grad Gamma(u).        (9)

Indeed the continuous derivative is
m_cont-y S-(A-epsilon f(Y)S)grad Gamma(u). This proves (9) without any body
variation or common-separator assumption.

There is a unique deepest mark at each deepest base. If two marks in one
fiber were deepest, strict own concavity of f and an attaining active cap
at their midpoint would contradict (7) and local strictness of its tail.

More strongly, no nontrivial convex combination of distinct deepest bases
can be an integer base. Suppose p=sum lambda_i p_i is integer, with at
least two distinct p_i and positive coefficients, and let
Y=sum lambda_i Y_i. Actual convex compatibility makes Y feasible. By (7)
it has depth at least Q, hence is deepest. For an attaining active N there,

    c_Q(N)=N.Y-epsilon f(Y)Gamma(u)
        <=sum lambda_i[N.Y_i-epsilon f(Y_i)Gamma(u)]
        <=c_Q(N).

All inequalities are equalities. Therefore the SAME geometric smoothed cap
is active at each Y_i. Its one positive S and base moment m_base must obey
(8) with every p_i, contradiction.

Consequently the deepest bases are precisely the vertices of an empty
lattice polytope: their convex hull contains no other integer points.
In particular they have distinct parity and their number is at most k(P),
which is at most 2^n.

## 4. Positive-width ACTUAL singleton cover

At each deepest source Y_i=(p_i,y_i), compact active-quantile minimization
and Caratheodory give at most d+1 active normals N_ij, normalized by
Gamma(u_ij)=1, and positive weights rho_ij with sum_j rho_ij=1, such that

    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=epsilon grad_x f(Y_i),
    c_ij=N_ij.Y_i-epsilon f(Y_i), Q_h(N_ij,c_ij)=Q.       (10)

There is one group per deepest base; NO occupied source-face grouping is
needed at positive width. On its own fiber the function

    sum_j rho_ij(N_ij.w-c_ij)-epsilon f(w)

is nonnegative, with its unique zero at Y_i. This follows from the own
first-order tangent inequality and strict concavity. Both possible
boundary zeros and second interior zeros are excluded by joining to Y_i.

For an actual convex physical field Phi and finite cap-normal velocities,
use the same actual bodies K_z(t) from the H companion note. Let
A_i(t)=sum_j rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij(t)), and define

 alpha_i(t)=min_(x in K_(p_i)(t))
 [sum_j rho_ij N_ij(t).(p_i,x)-sum_j rho_ij c_ij
                         -epsilon(t) A_i(t) f_t(p_i,x)].

Its unique old contact Y_i remains interior. The uniform signed energy
expansion gives alpha_i(t)=t alpha_i'+o(t), with the exact H coefficient
(15) from the H-response note, now at this SINGLE source. Solve the exact
smooth quantile equation

    sum_j rho_ij c_ij(t,q_i(t))
       =sum_j rho_ij c_ij+alpha_i(t).

It covers the ENTIRE current own source fiber by its selected smoothed
caps of mass at most q_i(t). The finite off-deepest-base gap persists.
Thus strict descent in every group gives actual global objective descent.
This is a positive-width cover, established before taking any limit.

The singleton property also legitimizes using the bounded clipped cap as
an ACTUAL menu member. Clipping preserves every old smoothed fiber mass,
its own threshold and hence its active status. It preserves u, so (10)
and the own-fiber contact budget remain exact. No projected resultant on
a multi-base contact face has to be preserved. This is stronger than the
mere bounded-record use of clipping in the archived general limit note.

## 5. Exact physical response, including width covariance

Let v_z be inward normal speed, D_z=integral_boundary v_z, D=sum D_z,
and use the H notation

    J_j=sum_z integral_boundary [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2 v_z dS,
    b_i=epsilon f(Y_i), C_E,i=integral_boundary K_pi P_i^(-d-1)v_pi.

For a fixed old cap j, let B_j(v)=integral_boundary Psi(q_j) v dS.
A normal velocity nu_j=(dot a_j,dot u_j), threshold velocity r_j, and the
actual covariance change give

    dot Gamma_j=(D-J_j)/(2M)+grad Gamma(u_j).dot u_j.

Direct differentiation of (2), including the moving body, gives the exact
captured-volume LOSS

    L_j=B_j(v)+S_j r_j-m_j.nu_j+A_j dot Gamma_j.          (11)

Thus define

    b_j^smooth(v)=B_j(v)+A_j(D-J_j)/(2M),
    m_j^eff=m_j-A_j(0,grad Gamma(u_j)).                  (12)

Then L_j=b_j^smooth+S_j r_j-m_j^eff.nu_j. The term A_j must not be dropped
at positive h. It is the response of the body-dependent smoothing width.

Put B_i=sum_j rho_ij/S_j. Equalizing the actual smooth cap losses, with
sum rho_ij r_j=alpha_i', gives the exact group loss

    l_i=[alpha_i'+sum_j rho_ij b_j^smooth/S_j
                    -sum_j rho_ij (m_j^eff/S_j).nu_j]/B_i.  (13)

At positive width this is LINEAR in every physical/normal/scale direction:
there is no hinge branch and no remaining contact minimum.

## 6. ONE positive-width separator and its exact density

Minimality forbids a direction with l_i-beta D>0 for every i. The actually
addable convex physical cone and arbitrary signed normal variables are
exactly those already constructed in the H companion note. Finite-dimensional
separation on any finite list of fields therefore gives lambda_i>=0,
sum lambda_i=1, whose averaged response is nonpositive on that cone and
zero on every signed normal variable. The compact simplex of lambdas and
the finite-intersection property give ONE lambda valid for all physical
fields simultaneously.

Set

    kappa_i=lambda_i/B_i, e_i=kappa_i b_i, Delta=sum_i e_i,
    omega_ij=kappa_i rho_ij/S_j,
    Abar=sum_ij omega_ij A_ij,
    W=sum_ij omega_ij Psi(q_ij) on each actual boundary.

Then sum omega_ij=1 and omega_ij S_ij=kappa_i rho_ij. The simultaneous
boundary density is

 Xi_h = W-beta
    +sum_(i:p_i=z)e_i[P_i^(-d-1)/((d+1)E_i)
                                  +1/(d(d+1)V_z)]
    +(1/(2M))sum_ij [e_i rho_ij-omega_ij A_ij]
                                      [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
    -(d+2)Delta/(2dM)+Abar/(2M).                         (14)

For every realized normal-dependent convex Phi,

    integral_boundary Xi_h Phi <=0.                     (15)

All coefficients in the positive source/covariance part of (14) are
nonnegative, because A_ij<=0. Thus the same positive normal-preserving
surface convex-order formulation is available already at positive width,
with target density

    beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM)-Abar/(2M).

The signed normal equations agree exactly with (8)--(9): for positive
omega, m_ij/S_ij=Y_i-[b_i-A_ij/S_ij](0,grad Gamma(u_ij)). Equation (8) is
true even for active caps of zero separator weight.

If an independently attained interior log-epsilon selection is used,
its scalar coefficient is still -Delta (h is held fixed), giving the
usual Delta=M tau. No such scale selection is required here.

Uniformly on the compact class, |Abar|<=h S_max and the difference between
(14) and its A_ij=0 expression is bounded in absolute value by C h on the
entire normal bundle. Also c epsilon<=Delta<=C epsilon. Therefore the
relative width error after division by Delta is O(h/epsilon). Choosing
h=o(epsilon) removes that error; it does not remove unknown cap selectors
or prove numerical payment.

## 7. Zero-width limits give linked inside/outside selectors

Fix epsilon and take h_l down to zero through attained smooth minima.
The compact body class, uniform finite cap/contact counts, bounded normal
representatives, simplex weights and source cores admit a common
subsequence. Formula (4) proves that the limiting body is an actual H
minimum and Q_l converges to its H maximal raw depth. Every limiting
selected cap has that raw mass: nonvertical boundaries have zero volume,
and smoothing error is O(h_l). Width corrections in (14) vanish.

For each selected cap retain the weak boundary-capture measure

    Psi(q_j,l) dS_(partial K_z,l)

and the weak smooth-section measure psi(q_j,l)dX/h_l. They are uniformly
bounded; the latter is supported in a vanishing plane slab. Convex-body
boundary measures on the normal bundle converge under positive Hausdorff
convergence. Limits have boundary density W_j in [0,1]. Away from the
limiting cutting plane this density is the usual zero/one capture.

The linkage is an exact Gauss--Green identity, not a guessed subgradient.
For a C^1 compact test phi in the continuous coordinates, at every width

 u_j,l integral_(K_z,l) phi psi(q_j,l)/h_l
   =integral_(partial K_z,l) phi Psi(q_j,l)n dS
                     -integral_(K_z,l) Psi(q_j,l) grad phi dX.  (16)

If the limiting cap is outside-supporting, its volume capture tends to
zero, and (16) gives section measure

    tau_j dS/|u_j| on its supporting facet,
    tau_j=W_j.                                          (17)

If it is inside-supporting, its volume capture tends to the whole body.
Subtract the ordinary Gauss--Green identity to obtain instead

    tau_j dS/|u_j|,
    tau_j=1-W_j.                                        (18)

A proper cut gives the ordinary full proper section coarea. Thus the
limiting physical capture is tau on OUTSIDE support and 1-tau on INSIDE
support, while its section selector is tau in both cases. Full captured
boundary parts away from the plane remain weighted1. No assumption that
body or plane deviations are O(h_l) was used.

All these allocations come from the SAME sequence and the SAME separator.
Passing (15) yields one coherent limiting separator with those linked
weights and the unmodified H source/covariance terms.

IMPORTANT LIMIT SCOPE: new deepest bases can appear at the limiting H
body. The retained singleton source menus need not cover those new bases.
Their limiting inequalities are justified by passing (15), NOT by
asserting a complete finite cover of every limiting deepest fiber.

## 8. The common kernel retains joint facet height geometry

Separate arbitrary L-infinity selectors would lose additional information.
First let F be the relative interior of one positive-area limiting fiber
facet, with outer normal n. On a compact convex subfacet F' inside F, the
SAME moving body boundary has the graph

    X+s_l(X)n,   X in F',

where s_l is concave and tends uniformly to zero. Its graph area densities
tend to1 locally: concavity and uniform convergence bound the tangential
slopes on every smaller compact subfacet. For any cap limiting to support
on F, its continuous normal tends to either +alpha n or -alpha n, with
alpha>0 fixed by Gamma normalization. Its exact boundary kernel argument is

    (u_j,l.n) s_l(X)/h_l + L_j,l(X),                    (19)

where L_j,l is affine. For an outside cap put tau_j,l=Psi(argument); for an
inside cap put tau_j,l=1-Psi(argument). By (1), BOTH cases have the form

    tau_j,l(X)=Psi(alpha_j,l r_l(X)+ell_j,l(X)),
    r_l=s_l/h_l CONCAVE, alpha_j,l>0, ell_j,l AFFINE.     (20)

The SAME r_l is used for every supporting cap on this fiber facet. The
affine functions and r_l may diverge; a bounded blow-up profile is not assumed.

For the uniform kernel, put g_j,l=1+alpha_j,l r_l+ell_j,l. Then

    tau_j,l=min(1,(g_j,l)_+),

and g_j,l is concave. The positive support {g_j,l>0} is convex, and tau_j,l
is concave ON THAT SUPPORT. No global concavity of the zero extension to
the entire facet is asserted. Its exact one-height lift is the convex set

    L_j,l={(X,t): X in F', 0<=t<=1, t<=g_j,l(X)}.         (21)

Its t-fiber length is tau_j,l, apart from harmless zero-height fibers.
Hence the selector is a genuine 1-concave density, not merely a
quasiconcave function. Hausdorff subsequences of the bounded convex lifts
in (21) give L1 convergence of their indicator functions, and therefore
L1 convergence of their height densities. This works also when the limit
has zero volume. Thus limiting selectors admit concave-on-positive-support
representatives and actual convex one-height lifts locally on the facet.
Exhaust the relative facet interior by compact convex subfacets. In d=1
facets are points and these assertions have their scalar interpretation.

For the optional smooth kernel, (20) still makes every selector
quasiconcave. L1 precompactness follows by extracting convex superlevel sets
at rational levels and sandwiching outside their measure-zero boundaries.
The uniform-kernel lift is a strictly stronger conclusion.

### 8.1 One FULL physical roof, including sampled boundary bases

When the limiting facet is an ambient facet of the canonical hull, this
structure is joint in the BASE and continuous facet variables. Write its
supporting plane as

    a_F.z+n_F.x=b_F,  n_F!=0,

choose the continuous transverse direction e=n_F/|n_F|, and parametrize
the plane by affine physical coordinates (z,tangent x). For the ACTUAL
canonical C_l, its upper boundary in the e direction is one concave roof
s_l(z,tangent x), wherever that vertical projection is defined.

Do NOT discard sampled bases on the boundary of the projected ambient
facet. They may have positive own-facet area while being ambient-surface
null. Instead, at EACH of the finitely many sampled bases carrying such a
facet, choose a compact patch inside the relative interior of its OWN
facet. Positive-fiber Hausdorff convergence ensures that the common upper
roof is defined on every patch for large l: each vertical line also has a
uniformly inward point in its limiting positive fiber. Fiberwise convergence
makes the roof tend uniformly to zero there. Convexity makes its domain
contain the convex hull G of all these sampled patches. Its concavity
supplies a lower bound tending to zero throughout G, while ambient Hausdorff
convergence and the limiting supporting plane give the upper bound tending
to zero. Thus this is one actual jointly concave roof on G, including the
original sampled boundary bases.

For a cap supporting any of these parallel own facets, (19)--(20) hold
with ell_j,l AFFINE IN ALL (z,tangent x) variables. The continuous normal
orientation fixes whether its section selector is W or 1-W. The uniform
lift (21), with G replacing F', is then a convex set in

    (base z, continuous tangent x, added height t).

Its sampled traces satisfy every actual anchored Minkowski inclusion.
Take Hausdorff subsequences of the traces at EVERY finite occupied sampled
base, separately if necessary; their anchored inclusions pass to the
limit, and their volumes converge even for degenerate limiting traces.
This retains the boundary-base fibers rather than replacing their mixed
measure by an ambient integral. Restrict to compact patches and anchored
combinations actually lying in G; exhaust larger facet pieces as needed.
No gluing of distinct ambient facets is asserted.

### 8.2 Cross-cap constraints from the same roof

All the lifts just constructed use the SAME concave roof and differ only
by their positive coefficients and affine corrections. Retaining their
joint graph measures records simultaneous provenance; arbitrary independent
concave selectors are not asserted to be attainable. At finite width,
where both selector values lie strictly between0 and1,

    Psi^(-1)(tau_j,l)/alpha_j,l
      -Psi^(-1)(tau_k,l)/alpha_k,l

is affine in the full facet coordinates. For the uniform kernel,
Psi^(-1)(t)=t-1 on (0,1). A limiting inverse formula requires an unsaturated
region; none is asserted globally at values0 or1.

Equal normalized continuous normals give kernel arguments differing only
by a basewise constant, so ordering their offsets orders their boundary
weights on that fiber. Exactly opposite normalized continuous normals give
q_j+q_k=s_z constant there. Then

    s_z>=-1 implies W_j+W_k>=1,
    s_z<=-1 implies W_j+W_k<=1,
    s_z=-1 implies W_j+W_k=1.                            (22)

For a complementary geometric pair s_z=0; its outside and inside section
selectors therefore satisfy tau_out>=tau_in. These conclusions survive
limits when the stated finite-width relations or uniform scaled inequalities
persist. Coincidence/opposition of LIMITING normals alone does not control
their differences divided by h_l, and does not identify their selectors.

A necessary remaining distinction is saturation: (21) is an INDIVIDUAL
convex lift for each cap selector. In coordinates of the common roof,
its height is a cap-dependent slab truncation, equivalently a difference
of two nested tail heights. These formulas do NOT identify all selectors
as ordinary halfspace caps of one bounded common convex body. At each
finite width a common lower floor can be chosen on compact G, but that
floor and the resulting body's volume may diverge as h tends to zero.
No common-floor budget or single-cap realization is supplied here.

### 8.3 Individual selector concavity does not repair the facet exponent

For d>=2, a concave positive selector tau times a positive affine facet
weight gives g=tau L^(-d). The automatic inverse-power property is only

    g^(-1/(d-1))=L^(d/(d-1)) tau^(-1/(d-1)) CONVEX.

This is the convex perspective power, decreasing in tau; composing with
concave tau preserves convexity. Its exponent d-1 equals the facet
dimension and is below the radial-centering threshold d.

There is an exact obstruction to silently upgrading the exponent. On
0<=x<=1 take L=1+x and tau=(1+x/2)/2, an unsaturated affine [0,1] selector
in (20) with constant roof. Then for every beta>=d,

    (d^2/dx^2) [g^(-1/beta)] at x=0
       =2^(1/beta) [(d-1/2)^2+beta(-d+1/4)]/beta^2 <0.

At beta=d the numerator is (1-3d)/4, and it decreases thereafter.
Thus individual uniform-kernel lift concavity does not by itself supply
the admissible inverse-power facet law. The shared roof and actual source
moments remain additional information; this scalar test does not impose
the full critical menu conditions.
